identity.title: Less is Enough: Synthesizing Diverse Data in LLM Feature Space with Sparse Autoencoders

problem.claim: How to construct diverse post-training data whose diversity reflects task-relevant LLM features.

gap.claim: Text-based diversity metrics capture linguistic variation but provide weak signals for task-relevant features linked to downstream performance.

contributions.claim: Feature Activation Coverage (FAC), a diversity measure defined in an interpretable feature space.
FAC Synthesis, which uses a sparse autoencoder to identify missing seed-data features and generates synthetic samples reflecting them.
The authors report a shared interpretable feature space across LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen that enables cross-model knowledge transfer.

stated_novelty.claim: The work introduces FAC and the FAC Synthesis framework for feature-space-guided diversity measurement and data synthesis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent improvements in data diversity and downstream performance across instruction following, toxicity detection, reward modeling, and behavior steering tasks.
The authors report that the shared interpretable feature space across LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen enables cross-model knowledge transfer.

narrative_sequence.summary: Post-training data diversity is presented as important for downstream LLM performance.
Existing text-based diversity metrics are described as weak indicators of task-relevant features.
The paper introduces FAC and uses it in FAC Synthesis, combining sparse-autoencoder feature discovery with feature-targeted sample generation.
The authors report gains in diversity and downstream performance across four task categories, plus cross-model feature-space transfer.

source_observation.claim: The paper aligns its diversity metric with an interpretable feature space and then uses the same feature representation to guide synthesis.

lessons.interpretation: A metric can become more actionable when it directly specifies what the generation procedure should cover.
lessons.application: Define a measurable coverage target in the representation used to diagnose missing data, then condition synthesis on that target.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the representation is not interpretable, task-relevant, or reliable across the intended models.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative effect sizes, statistical uncertainty, or synthesis cost.
It does not detail how FAC is computed, how missing features are selected, or how cross-model transfer is evaluated.
